title: model-specific-runtime-optimizations-llama-mistral-qwen-gqa-mqa-tuning
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: We observed model-specific performance regressions and suboptimal kernel choices for Llama/Mistral/Qwen under MQA/GQA configs and continuous batching workloads. This PR introduces targeted heuristics and micro-optimizations: (1) improved kernel selection for grouped-quantization (GQA) and multi-quantization (MQA) variants to avoid pathological GEMM layouts; (2) fused rotary/GQA path for Llama to reduce tensor transformations; (3) KV-cache compaction and eviction heuristics for Mistral variable-length contexts to improve steady-state throughput; (4) Qwen attention rotary correction to avoid extra copies when using 8-bit kernels; (5) continuous-batching padding-aware scheduler that reorders small requests to increase packing efficiency without violating latency SLOs. Changes are guarded behind feature flags and unit-tested. Summary of user-visible impact: +8-18% throughput on Mistral family models under mixed-length workloads, 5-12% reduction in p99 latency for Llama MQA runs, and 3-7% cost per token reduction for Qwen in 8-bit configurations. See benchmark section below for test harness and numbers.

diff_highlights: runtime/kernel_selector.rs: new heuristic that prefers stride-major GEMM for GQA when group_size%64==0; avoids expensive transpose for 4-bit layouts
runtime/attention/llama_fused.rs: added fused rotary+quantized matmul path (LLAMA_FUSED_ROTARY flag); reduces intermediate allocations
runtime/kv_cache/mistral_compaction.rs: compaction algorithm that consolidates small KV segments and updates index mapping to avoid cache blowup
runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.rs: padding-aware reorderer that groups similar-seqlen requests within 5ms window
runtime/attention/qwen_rotary_fix.rs: change avoids extra copy when using 8-bit kernels by applying rotary in-place and updating kernel inputs
benchmarks: Qwen-7B 8-bit streaming: cost/token -3.9% with in-place rotary and kernel selection
Continuous-batcher packing efficiency: average batch occupancy from 62% -> 78%
